objectives.text: State the word equation for photosynthesis: carbon dioxide + water -> glucose + oxygen
successCriteria: I can place carbon dioxide and water on the left of the word equation and glucose and oxygen on the right
I can name light energy trapped by chlorophyll as the energy input over the arrow
assessmentPoints: Partner answers in the opening activity
Word equations written in the closing worksheet activity

objectives.text: Explain where carbon dioxide and water enter the plant, and where glucose and oxygen go
successCriteria: I can trace carbon dioxide in through the pores under the leaf and water up from the roots
I can say glucose stays as the plant food while oxygen is released into the air
assessmentPoints: Route tracing answers during the raw-materials activity
Closing worksheet answers on the raw-materials question

objectives.text: Explain why the released oxygen comes from water, not from carbon dioxide
successCriteria: I can state that splitting water releases the oxygen
I can state that carbon dioxide supplies the carbon for glucose instead
assessmentPoints: Responses when the trap is sprung
Exit ticket answers on the oxygen-source question

activities.title: Meet the leaf and name the inputs and products
Trace the two raw materials to the leaf
Follow the products out of the leaf

differentiation.support: Provide the word equation with the arrow and energy input pre-drawn so learners place the four substances.

activities.title: Energy in, food out: plants as producers
Spring the oxygen-source trap, worksheet and exit ticket

differentiation.stretch: Ask learners to explain, using the split water, why the oxygen cannot come from the carbon dioxide.
